title: Built-in herd registry defaults and per-agent env
action: Per D3: agent_registry(cfg) in wave.rs starts from built-in defaults — claude-sonnet => [claude,--model,sonnet,--permission-mode,bypassPermissions], agy-flash => [agy,--dangerously-skip-permissions] — then overlays config entries (same name overrides). UnknownAgent 'known' listing therefore always includes the built-ins. Per D4: a registry entry value may also be an object {"argv": [...], "env": {"KEY":"value"}}: argv validated exactly like the array shape; env keys must match [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, values must be newline-free — any violation drops the whole entry (fail-open-per-entry, matching the existing rule). Registry value type becomes a small struct (argv + env BTreeMap); resolve_agent_command returns the env alongside (kind, args) — adjust its two callers. In run.rs execute_new: when env is non-empty, AFTER the pane split and BEFORE agent start, send one line `export K='v' K2='v2'` (single-quote values, escape embedded single quotes as '\'') into the pane through a new Herdr trait method pane_run(pane_id, command) implemented with `herdr pane run <pane> <command>` (check `herdr pane run --help` for exact argv and use it; if it needs different plumbing use send-text+send-keys Enter). A pane_run failure is a typed spawn failure that closes the just-split pane (same rule as a start failure). Wave/control-loop callers that spawn panes apply the same env line when they split+start; callers that only brief running agents do not. Extend FakeHerdr + PanicHerdr; tests: object-shape entry parses with env; bad env key or newline value drops the entry; export line is sent before agent_start exactly when env is non-empty (order asserted), never sent for array-shape entries; built-in names resolve with zero config and are overridden by same-name config entries. Update .bee/config-sample-cli-executors.json to show one object-shape entry with env in its herding.agents plus a _doc line.

truths: agy-flash and claude-sonnet resolve with no herding config at all; config same-name entries override
Object-shape registry entry carries env; export line lands in the pane before agent start and only when env is non-empty
Invalid env key or value drops that entry only, never the registry

trace.outcome: Seeded built-in herd registry defaults (claude-sonnet, agy-flash) overridable by config, and added per-agent env carried through resolve_agent_command into a pane export line sent before agent start

report.outcome: agent_registry(cfg) now starts from built-in claude-sonnet/agy-flash defaults then overlays config.herding.agents entries (same-name override); a herding.agents value may be an object {argv, env} with env validated per-key/value, any violation dropping the whole entry; resolve_agent_command returns (kind, args, env); execute_new sends a sorted, single-quoted export line into the freshly split pane via a new Herdr::pane_run before agent_start, closing the pane on failure like a start failure; the wave.rs control-loop caller resolves env but documents in a code comment why it cannot apply it (HerdrBackend spawns via a different out-of-scope crate with no pane-split step in this file); config-sample-cli-executors.json gained an object-shape codex-envd example plus a _doc entry explaining both shapes and the env rules
report.tests: PATH="${CARGO_HOME:-$HOME/.cargo}/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml herding — green, 0 failed (5 interleaved FAILED lines are the pre-existing control_loop::tests::quick_exit_helper self-exec subprocess intentionally exercising its failure path, unrelated to this cell and unchanged by it; overall cargo test process exit code 0) — scope: herding suite covers registry defaults, resolution, and spawn/env-order, all 12 new tests passing
deviations: wave.rs build_wave_backend_and_run (the wave/control-loop resolve_agent_command caller) does not apply env: it never splits a pane itself, and the agent-start call for its HerdrBackend lives in packages/bee-rs/crates/fleet/src/backend/herdr.rs, a different crate outside this cell's file scope — documented in a code comment at the call site rather than reached past the boundary
